persona: Curious guest over 60 who needs clear names and repeats
reasons: Hugh says he was inside at 6:45 using the service clock, but the independently logged curtain was locked from 6:38 until 7:00. The fast brass clock cannot explain his stated time.
He leans against a brass corner post. The actual 6:31 installation photo shows open steel supports and no brass cabinet posts; his account fits the superseded proposal instead.
Several other guests give impossible late times, and several others describe obsolete cabinet features during earlier visits. Hugh is the one whose account fails both comparisons.
His financial exposure and business around the salon fit an incentive and possible opportunity, although the physical toxin evidence does not individually identify him.
confusion: An innocent player receiving my false sliding-glass account needs a clear private explanation of why they are telling that story and how to answer a follow-up without improvising a contradiction.
I need a clear distinction between what I know privately, what I must read, and what I can admit before Coming Clean.
The stage II accounts repeat 'Near the toast I was outside...' and 'My other business...' too often; they feel assembled rather than spoken.
A real table read aloud will be harder to compare than this persistent transcript, especially with sixteen guests and unfamiliar names.
improvements: Provide a neutral host-led chance to request a repeat of any witness account after the final evidence arrives; do not supply a solution-focused notes grid.
Explain innocent cover stories privately in character-specific terms and give short safe responses to obvious challenges.
Vary sentence order, vocabulary and rhythm across witnesses, while retaining the same evidentiary information.
Share large, clearly dated versions of both display images so older guests can distinguish actual installation from discarded proposal.
A human rehearsal is needed to determine whether the auditory memory burden makes this fair rather than simply harder.
accidental_solution_giveaways: No confession is accidentally read in the provided stages.

Once the final records arrive, the shared sentence template makes the late-time plus obsolete-feature combination easy to scan. This remains a recognizable deduction pattern for a reader with the full transcript.
experience: The first round feels broad and suspicious. The second round adds several dishonest witnesses rather than one obvious liar. The final pictures and independent records allow a reasoned accusation, though the unique overlap remains fairly easy to identify with a persistent transcript. I would enjoy examining the images, but I would want names repeated at a dinner table.
limitations: Independent guest assessment of scripted sixteen-character testimony; not a live interactive game. No Coming Clean material or organizer was read.
